title: Hosted API onboarding flow with technical readiness checks and fallback matrices
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit hosted API feature requests that mix streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Some combinations are not production-ready (e.g., high-throughput streaming + large KV caches + third-party toolchains) and lead to inconsistent latency/costs or failed rollouts. Currently intake is manual and inconsistent across PMs/SEs.

Goal: Create a deterministic onboarding flow that applies automated technical readiness checks, produces a weighted eligibility score, and generates a fallback matrix mapping requested features to supported rollouts and SLA tiers. The flow should:
- Surface incompatibilities early (latency, model variant, quantization, KV cache size).
- Produce a clear fallback plan (e.g., degrade streaming to polling, downgrade model to lower-cost variant, disable toolchain calls) tied to customer SLA tiers.
- Provide an audit trail and handoff artifact for Sales/SEs and Eng to implement.

Success criteria: new enterprise intake reduces manual clarifications by 60% for complex feature requests and enables a supported rollout plan within 3 business days for 80% of cases.
in_scope: Automated questionnaire for enterprise feature intake (streaming, tool/function calling, structured outputs)
Technical readiness check engine (latency, sequence length, KV cache size, model compatibility matrix)
Weighted eligibility scorer and threshold rules per SLA tier
Fallback matrix generator that maps requested capabilities to mitigation actions
Console export (PDF/MD) for handoff and audit logs
out_of_scope: Billing / pricing model changes for committed capacity
acceptance_criteria: Intake form captures all signals required by the readiness checks (latency SLO, expected QPS, max token length, tool call dependencies)
Readiness engine returns an eligibility score and explicit explanations for flags in >95% of test requests
Fallback matrix produces at least one viable mitigation path per flagged incompatibility
SE/PM pilot with 6 enterprise requests shows 60% fewer clarification cycles vs baseline
Handoff artifact added to Console as downloadable package and to ticket as link
notes: Trade-offs discussed: run checks synchronously during intake vs. asynchronously with a status webhook. We chose synchronous for immediate feedback for high-risk enterprise requests (P1/P0), with an async fallback for very long-running diagnostics. We also scoped the first iteration to Hosted API only (no VPC/private).
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Raman: Kickoff with SEs and Solutions. Collected 12 sample enterprise requests that previously failed rollouts. Initial questionnaire draft attached to Confluence.

2025-02-27 - Luca Moretti: Architecture sync with ENG. Agreed on minimal readiness checks: model-compatibility table, estimated peak token rate, KV cache threshold, and tool-call outbound connectivity matrix. ENG will expose a /readiness API (see ENG-58210).
2025-03-03 - Design review: Mockups for Console handoff artifact presented. Feedback: make mitigation steps human-readable and include cost delta estimates.

2025-03-07 - PM triage: Decided to prioritize SLA-tiered thresholds (enterprise tiers 1-3). For Tier 1, require automated checks to pass before scheduling on-prem/privates. For Tier 3, allow manual approval with advisory flags.
2025-03-10 - SE pilot: Ran 4 live intake forms; readiness engine correctly flagged 3 and suggested fallbacks. One false-positive on KV cache sizing; ENG to refine heuristics.
2025-03-12 - Luca Moretti: Pushed initial readiness-engine branch to GH. Created ENG PR #468 (readiness engine skeleton). Next: integrate console export and add cost delta calc.
